newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU covers Saudi barley deal in record time.
newsitem.headline: EU covers Saudi barley deal in record time.

text.p: The European Union wrapped up the lion's share of the latest Saudi barley purchase in record time on Thursday, releasing almost 300,000 tonnes towards the deal at $132 per tonne Fob, EU grain officials said.
The award of 296,000 tonnes, at refunds up to 29.97 Ecus, brings to 1.6 million tonnes the amount of barley released for the world market in the past six weeks.
Of this, at least 350,000 to 400,000 tonnes is currently expected to meet Saudi Arabia's latest purchase of 500,000 tonnes of optional origin on Wednesday, officials said.
The rest would come from Canada.
The EU move was a quickfire response to Saudi Arabia's purchase of barley to be delivered in late April and May, at prices generally estimated between $152 and $154 a tonne.
Traders estimate freight and other costs to be deducted from this at around $22 per tonne.
"We gave 300,000 tonnes today which is a very unusual award for the end of the season and we covered extremely quickly," a European Union grain official said.
"The bids (for subsidies) were very good today so we were very interested," he said.
The EU had held its implied barley export price at around $130 per tonne in previous export tenders.
The official said it was also sensible to respond quickly to a deal concluded at the end of the season. Officials and traders pointed out that delivery schedules were tight.
The rapid pace at which the deal was pieced together by four companies contrasted with gruelling negotiations following Saudi Arabia's previous purchase of 1.2 million tonnes in January.
Freight sources on Thursday reported 90,000 tonnes fixed for Jeddah from northern France on April 20-25 and there was talk that 50,000 tonnes had been booked to leave from Vancouver.
Saudi Arabia bought the barley in what traders regarded as a stop-gap tender to ensure smooth supplies ahead of a Moslem holiday, pending possible further purchases in May.
